'''Xenu's paradox''' was the paradoxical statement&mdash;attributed to [[Xenu]]&mdash;that no matter how fast an object or person traveled, it would be unable to close the gap between itself and another object. During the [[Battle of Skye|battle]] of [[Skye/Legends|Skye]], [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Halagad Ventor]] was reminded of the paradox while chasing [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Zeta Magnus]] through the corridors of [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Kharys' fortress|citadel]].

==Behind the scenes==
Xenu's paradox was first mentioned in ''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]'', by [[Abel G. Peña]]. The concept and the name of the paradox closely resemble [[Wikipedia:Zeno's paradoxes#Achilles and the tortoise|one of Zeno's paradoxes]], attributed to the ancient real-world philosopher [[Wikipedia:Zeno of Elea|Zeno]].
